newsitem.title: UK: UK government seeks views on gene crops.
newsitem.headline: UK government seeks views on gene crops.

text.p: The British government has invited public comments on the use of genetically modified herbicide resistant crops, food industry minister Lord Donoughue announced on Thursday.
Ministers wanted to hear the views of those with an interest before the new crops start to become commercially available in the UK in 1998, the ministry of agriculture said in a statement.
A new discussion paper "Weed Control on the Farm: Management of Genetically Modified Herbicide Tolerant Crops," examines the use of these crops, the ministry said.
"The Government has not taken a view either way on this subject. We are keen to hear the views of consumers, environmentalists, scientists, the industry and independent advisory committees," he said.
